## TL;DR

Healthy running-task cards show their state without the repetitive “active N ago” suffix. Board and Pipeline recency is available through the shared tooltip on mouse hover and keyboard focus. Silent/stuck tasks retain their inline signal and elapsed time; idle review and close-out rows retain time in state. Touch-specific tooltip pinning was removed after repeated gesture arbitration edge cases, as directed in review 7.

## Work and rationale

TaskCard keeps the active state label concise and includes last-activity timing in its tooltip. The checks and confirming-handoff status paths expose the same recency, including when the check-progress component renders instead of the standard hint. Silent and stuck states keep their useful inline signal. PipelineView supplies the agent’s last-activity timestamp separately from task `updated_at`, and PipelineCard uses that timestamp for healthy live-work tooltips.

The shared status resolver now evaluates the established prolonged-silence threshold before the generic running-process fallback. Handoff/check activity and queue state keep priority, while a stale “running” process no longer hides the Stuck state. Pipeline hides elapsed time only while healthy work is actively in flight and a recency tooltip replaces that time. Stuck, idle review, and close-out rows retain elapsed/state duration.

Regression tests cover concise coding labels, hover and focus tooltip display, confirming-handoff timing, check-progress timing, the PipelineView timestamp wiring, silent-but-running status, elapsed retention for review/close-out, and shared PipelineCard tooltip behavior. The Pipeline portion remains in this bundle because it is the same recency presentation across the two task views and has focused tests.

## Approaches tried

Reviews 5 and 6 identified missing timing on checks/confirming-handoff, an incorrect Pipeline timestamp source, stuck-state precedence, and elapsed time disappearing from unrelated rows. The current worktree already included fixes for those paths; I added explicit confirming-handoff coverage and an integration-level PipelineView test to ensure actual agent activity, rather than an old `updated_at`, reaches the tooltip. I also added a full PipelineView-to-PipelineCard test for a silent task whose process still reports running.

Review 7 directed removing the global touch tap-to-pin and long-press behavior. I restored `tooltip.ts` to the current `main` implementation, removed the task-specific touch attributes and touch gesture tests, and added hover/focus assertions for the recency hint. Touch now follows the shared tooltip’s existing behavior and a tap proceeds to the element’s normal click action.

## Challenges and blockers

The earlier touch implementation tried to arbitrate between pinned tooltips and clickable cards. Repeated review rounds found edge cases around switching triggers, dismissing a pinned tip, and allowing the underlying action. Continuing to add gesture rules would have expanded a small UI bundle and risked changing clicks across the application. Following review 7’s direction removes that behavior and keeps the task focused on mouse and keyboard access. The task’s original touch-pinning acceptance has therefore been dropped at the reviewer’s instruction.

A changed-path check started during the preceding turn but was interrupted when new review messages arrived. The final run completed after the touch behavior was removed. The first remote host hung and RepoOS retried on `bee`; the retry built the branch and passed all 5,082 selected tests, with one skipped. Local format, lint, build, CSS/theme guards, rendered contrast, and UI smoke checks passed.

## Key learnings

Status text, activity recency, and elapsed state time are related but serve different cases. Healthy live work can move recency into a tooltip; silence should remain visible in the line; and idle review/close-out rows need duration even without agent activity. Touch gestures can interact with nested clickable cards in several ways, and the repeated arbitration fixes were adding complexity beyond this small bundle. Restoring the shared tooltip to its existing touch behavior keeps task-specific changes confined to recency presentation. Mouse hover and keyboard focus continue to reveal details, while touch taps retain their prior action semantics.
